question: Should OpenClaw core own durable signed ClawHub publisher-feed state and refresh scheduling, and if so what is the approved landing order for the verification, transport, state, and follow-management layers?
rationale: The proposed work creates a persistent remote-content trust and storage surface across several unmerged PRs; implementation quality alone cannot determine the intended permanent core-versus-extension boundary.

options.title: Approve a staged core stack
options.body: Confirm the core ownership and merge the verifier, transport, durable-state, then follow-management layers only after each layer has targeted upgrade and live-runtime proof.

options.title: Move the capability out of core
options.body: Keep core limited to generic plugin/catalog seams and direct publisher-feed discovery, persistence, and refresh to a ClawHub plugin or external owner.

options.title: Pause for protocol finalization
options.body: Hold these draft PRs until the referenced feed protocol and producer implementation have an explicit maintainer-approved consumer contract.

recommendation.title: Approve a staged core stack
recommendation.body: Confirm the core ownership and merge the verifier, transport, durable-state, then follow-management layers only after each layer has targeted upgrade and live-runtime proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor is the only identified person connected across the proposed feed stack, although a repository owner must make the product decision.
